O1.citation: “The run is invalid. Seeing the bar breaks blindness... Discard the artifact and any grades derived from it.”

O2.citation: “Start a fresh, context-free runner. Give it only the case input and the instruction to use the target skill” and “Grade the new artifact with a separate judge that sees only the artifact, bar, and skill first principles.”

O3.citation: “Remove only attributable deltas” while preserving “all pre-existing changes exactly, including changes in the same files”; uncertain changes must not be modified.

O4.citation: “Provide a throwaway writable directory if files are required” and afterward “compare the live checkout against the preserved baseline again and remove any newly attributable leakage.”

S1.citation: The smell is absent: the artifact says to “Discard the artifact and any grades derived from it.”

S2.citation: The smell is absent: it says “Stop the runner” and “Start a fresh, context-free runner.”

S3.citation: The smell is absent: “Do not use blanket commands such as `git reset --hard`, `git restore .`, or `git clean -fd`.”

S4.citation: The smell is absent: even after using a throwaway writable directory, it requires comparing the live checkout against the baseline again and removing attributable leakage.

rationale: The artifact correctly invalidates the contaminated result, prescribes a genuinely fresh runner and separate fresh judge, gives a surgical recovery process that protects unrelated work, and requires both throwaway execution storage and continued live-checkout sweeps. It neither recommends unsafe cleanup nor materially unnecessary work.
